title: Profiling hunt logbook: regression triage and canary comparisons
content:
Purpose:
This is a running logbook for diagnosing a recent regression in production request latency (noticed by Alert: serving.request_p99 > 450ms for 10m). The goal is to capture first impressions, hypotheses, commands we ran, quick mitigations, and an action plan for a deterministic bisect + canary comparison. This is intentionally informal — notes, half-done queries, and TODOs are expected.

Summary of what hit the wall:
- Alert symptom: sustained p99 latency spike for the hosted-text-generation route (route: /v1/generate) starting around 2025-11-02 02:13 UTC.
- Impact: small subset of customers (approx 0.6% of requests) observed increased p99 while p50 unchanged. Throughput and error rate stable.
- Immediate mitigation applied: reduced max-batch-size on the affected pool to 8 (was 16) to relieve queuing; reverted later after partial rollback.

Observed signals to check (quick checklist when paging someone):
- High-level metrics: request_count, request_duration (p50/p95/p99), queue_length, batch_size_distribution, GPU_utilization, memcpy bandwidth, host_cpu_idle.
- Runtime-specific: kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_evictions, kv_cache_latency, kv_cache_size_bytes.
- Serving runtime traces: trace_id sampling for p99 requests (pull traces from tracing/service).
- Canary vs baseline: use the canary job in infra/canaries/serving-latency to replay identical workload and collect p99 distributions.

Quick first-pass queries (PromQL-like pseudo):
- p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_serving_request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) by (route)
- queue length: sum(rate(redwood_serving_queue_length_sum[1m])) / sum(rate(redwood_serving_queue_length_count[1m]))
- batch size distribution: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(redwood_serving_batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)))
- GPU cuda memcpy: sum(rate(gpu_memcpy_bytes_total[1m])) by (device)

Key leads discovered so far (timeline entries):

2025-11-03 06:22 UTC — initial pager (Marcos)
- p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~480ms over 6 minutes. No change in error rate.
- Hypothesis: queuing/bunching + a slow tail kernel for certain sequence lengths.
- Immediately captured 50 p99 traces and saved snapshots to /tmp/latency-snapshots/2025-11-03-06.

2025-11-03 07:10 UTC — lightweight replay
- Replayed sampled requests (same model, same prompt size distribution) against a staging pool. p99 in staging stable. Suggests production-only condition (load skew or cache priming).

2025-11-03 08:01 UTC — profile capture on one affected host
- Commands run: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60, and pprof exported from the runtime's /debug/pprof/profile. Also collected nvprof on a single GPU card.
- Early flamegraph shows a noticeable increase in time spent in memcpy and attention kernel on sequences > 1024 tokens.

2025-11-03 09:30 UTC — KV cache hypothesis refined
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 0.82 to 0.57 for the route. Cache size metric showed evictions increased ~3x.
- Hypothesis: an upstream change (model variant or tokenization change) increased effective context window or caused more tokenization variance, reducing cache sharing.

Root-cause bisect plan (high level):
1) Narrow time window: 2025-11-01 to 2025-11-02 (when pre-rollout activity occurred).
2) Candidate planes: runtime commit range, model-variant push, routing policy change (split by region), infra change (driver/kernel update).
3) Bisect strategy: parallel canary runs of two variants — baseline (sha X) and candidate (sha Y) — with a replayed workload representative of real traffic (use sampler/recorder tool). Each run captures 1M tokens or 30 minutes, whichever first.
4) Compare: p50/p95/p99 and batch-size histogram plus kv_cache hit/evict counters. Use automated snapshot-diff tool to highlight percentiles delta.

Bisect playbook (commands & artifacts):
- Start recorder: ./tools/recorder --route /v1/generate --duration 30m --out samples/nov02.replay
- Deploy baseline: infra/deploy --version sha:X --pool canary-a --config canary-config-small
- Deploy candidate: infra/deploy --version sha:Y --pool canary-b --config canary-config-small
- Run replay (simultaneous): ./tools/replayer --input samples/nov02.replay --target canary-a --concurrency 12 & ./tools/replayer --input samples/nov02.replay --target canary-b --concurrency 12
- Collect metrics: ./tools/metrics-scrape --prom-url $PROM --match redwood_serving_* --out metrics/shaX-v-shaY-$(date +%s).json
- Diff: tools/snapshot-diff metrics/fileX metrics/fileY --report diff-report.html

Profiling tips (what to capture and why):
- Flamegraphs from perf/pprof: shows host-side CPU hot paths. Look for memcpy, path through RPC stack, and any blocking syscalls (futex).
- nvprof / Nsight: capture kernel durations and cudaMemcpy; look for increased memcpy times indicating memory-bound behavior.
- Runtime internal tracers: capture operator-level timings (attention, matmul, softmax) and KV cache lookup latencies.
- Sampling traces for p99: attach trace IDs to metric spikes to get full spans (router->proxy->worker->gpu-kernel).

Canary comparison checklist (metrics to compare side-by-side):
- request_duration p50/p95/p99
- queue_length and avg_queue_wait_ms
- batch_size percentiles and distribution shapes
- kv_cache hit_rate and eviction_rate
- gpu_utilization and per-kernel time breakdown
- host_cpu_steal & context switches
- memcpy bytes/sec and memcpy time per request

Experimental quick-fixes to validate hypotheses (non-prod first):
- Force smaller max_batch_size on candidate pool and re-run replay. If p99 improves -> queuing/bunching.
- Increase kv_cache_size (if possible) on candidate and observe hit_rate.
- Pin CPU governor to performance on worker host to see if host scheduling causes tail latency.
- If kernel-level hotspot suspected, try a different kernel selection (quantization profile fallback) or disable one optimization flag and re-evaluate.

Notes on observability and dashboarding improvements (follow-ups):
- Dashboard gap: there is no quick view of kv_cache hit_rate per-route with accompanying eviction_count. Add a small panel under infra/serving-runtime/kv-cache to correlate with latency.
- Add a p99-by-sequence-length heatmap (sequence_length buckets vs p99) so we can detect tail behavior for large contexts.
- Capture batch composition (prompt tokens vs generated tokens) as separate histograms.

Action items (assigned):
- [Marcos] finish bisect run with sha:X vs sha:Y and upload snapshot diff (due 2025-11-18).
- [Priya] add kv_cache per-route panel to Grafana and instrument eviction reasons (due 2025-11-20).
- [Sophia] run full-profile on 3 affected hosts and drop pprof + Nsight captures in gs://redwood-perf/nov03/ (due 2025-11-15).
- [Ethan] try a targeted canary with kv_cache_size doubled for pool-3 and report results (due 2025-11-16).

Open questions / things to remember:
- Was there a prod-only config flip or a traffic-shaping rule applied around 2025-11-02? Check infra change log and deployment audit.
- Is tokenizer change included in the model-variant pushed the week prior? Tokenization variance can wreak havoc on KV reuse.
- Are we observing the regression only in specific regions/instance types? Need to tabulate p99 by region/instance-type.

Attachments / snippets:
- Sample trace span for a slow p99 request (trace-id: 01f3a2): spans show heavy wait in proxy->batcher for 120ms followed by 90ms kernel time on GPU.
- pprof top snippet: memcpy: 34%, attention_kernel: 22%, runtime_dispatch: 14%
- nvprof summary: average memcpy HtoD increased by 2.2x for long sequences (>1024).

Concluding notes (for whoever picks this up next):
- This looks like a composition: increased cache churn + increased memcpy for certain sequences -> more queuing for a subset of requests -> p99 tail. The bisect is the highest-value next step. Keep replays deterministic and compare identical inputs.
- Keep an eye out for correlated config changes (autoscaler updates, kernel driver rolls, or model tokenization changes).

Scratch / raw commands used during the hunt (grabbed from shell history):
- promql: curl -s "${PROM}/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99%2Csum(rate(redwood_serving_request_duration_bucket[5m]))by(le%2Croute))by(route)" | jq .
- perf record: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60; sudo perf script > perf.script; flamegraph.pl perf.script > perf.svg
- pprof export: curl -s http://worker-host:6060/debug/pprof/profile > out.pprof; go tool pprof -http=:8081 out.pprof
- nvprof capture: sudo nvprof --profile-child-processes -o nvprof.nvvp ./bin/serving-worker --config worker.conf
- replay: ./tools/replayer --input samples/nov02.replay --target canary-a --concurrency 12 --report json > replayer-a.json

If you take this on: update the top-of-doc summary with final conclusion and move status -> in_review or final. Leave raw captures in gs://redwood-perf/nov03/ and link them in linked_artifacts.

End of logbook entry.
